newsitem.title: USA: US DOE not ready on Colorado gas reserves sale.
newsitem.headline: US DOE not ready on Colorado gas reserves sale.

text.p: U.S. Energy Secretary Federico Pena said Thursday the administration was not ready to propose selling or leasing natural gas reserves at the Naval Oil Shale Reserves in Colorado.
Appearing at a Senate Appropriations subcommittee hearing, Pena said the Energy Department is having preliminary discussions on how to go about selling or leasing the reserves.
But he said, "We're not at the stage of proposing legislation to sell the oil shale reserves."

Pena said he would be able to discuss the issue more after the department releases a report in September that assesses all of the federal oil and gas reserves, including the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
The Energy Department was to evaluate selling the Naval Oil Shale Reserves at the same time it was studying selling the Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve in California.
Pena in his prepared remarks said the department "is on track for completion of the Elk Hills sale as set forth by statute."
Under a 1996 law, the Elk Hills reserve near Bakersfield, California is to be sold no later than February 10, 1998.
